rule: I am · He / She / It is · You / We / They are

ex.en: I am a student.
She is my sister.
They are at home.
It is very hot today.
Are you ready?

q.s: My father ___ a doctor.
We ___ good friends.
I ___ from Bangladesh.
___ she your teacher?
The books ___ on the table.

bnsub: am, is, are: “হওয়া” বা “থাকা” বোঝাতে
expbn: কেউ কী, কে বা কেমন আছে বলতে am / is / are লাগে। বাংলায় অনেক সময় এই ক্রিয়াটা লুকানো থাকে (“আমি ছাত্র”), কিন্তু ইংরেজিতে বাদ দেওয়া যায় না।
I এর সাথে am, he / she / it বা একজনের সাথে is, আর you / we / they বা অনেকের সাথে are।
rulebn: I am · He / She / It is · You / We / They are
sub: Saying what someone or something is
exp: Use am, is or are to say who someone is, what something is, or how someone is. In Bangla this verb is often left out, but in English you always need it: I am a student.
Use am with I. Use is with he, she, it or one person or thing. Use are with you, we, they or more than one.

rule: a + consonant sound (a book) · an + vowel sound (an apple) · the = the one we both know

ex.en: I have a cat.
She eats an apple every day.
The cat is sleeping.
It takes an hour.
Close the door, please.

q.s: I saw ___ elephant at the zoo.
He is ___ engineer.
Please open ___ window. It's hot.
She bought ___ new phone.
We waited for ___ hour.

bnsub: a, an, the: কখন কোনটা
expbn: একটা যেকোনো জিনিস বোঝাতে a বা an। শব্দের শুরুর উচ্চারণ স্বরধ্বনি (a, e, i, o, u-এর শব্দ) হলে an, না হলে a।
নির্দিষ্ট, আগে বলা বা দুজনেই চেনে এমন জিনিস বোঝাতে the।
rulebn: a + ব্যঞ্জনধ্বনি (a book) · an + স্বরধ্বনি (an apple) · the = নির্দিষ্টটা
sub: Which one: a, an or the
exp: Use a or an for one thing when it doesn't matter which one. Use an before a vowel sound (an apple, an hour) and a before other sounds (a book, a university).
Use the when you and the listener know which one you mean: something you have already mentioned, or the only one there is.

rule: I / You / We / They work · He / She / It works · doesn't work

ex.en: I drink tea every morning.
She works in a bank.
The sun rises in the east.
He doesn't eat meat.
We go to the gym on Sundays.

q.s: My brother ___ football every evening.
They ___ in Chittagong.
She ___ like spicy food.
Water ___ at 100 degrees.
I ___ coffee at night.

bnsub: Simple present: অভ্যাস আর সাধারণ সত্য
expbn: যা নিয়মিত হয় বা সবসময় সত্য, তা বলতে simple present। যেমন রোজকার রুটিন।
he / she / it হলে ক্রিয়ার শেষে s বা es যোগ হয়। না-বোধক করতে don't / doesn't।
rulebn: I / You / We / They work · He / She / It works · doesn't work
sub: Habits and things that are always true
exp: Use the simple present for routines and habits (I drink tea every morning) and for facts that are always true (water boils at 100 degrees).
With he, she or it, add -s or -es to the verb: she works, he watches. For negatives use don't or doesn't + the base verb.

rule: am / is / are + verb-ing

ex.en: I am reading a book now.
She is cooking dinner.
They are playing outside.
It is raining.
What are you doing?

q.s: Look! The baby ___.
We ___ for the bus right now.
I ___ to music at the moment.
Why ___ you laughing?
He ___ TV now. He is studying.

bnsub: Present continuous: এখন যা চলছে
expbn: এই মুহূর্তে চলছে এমন কাজ বলতে am / is / are + ক্রিয়ার সাথে ing।
Look!, now, right now, at the moment এই শব্দগুলো দেখলে সাধারণত এটাই বসে।
rulebn: am / is / are + verb-ing
sub: Actions happening right now
exp: Use am, is or are + the verb with -ing for something happening at this moment: I am reading.
Words like now, right now, at the moment and Look! often go with this tense.

rule: worked / went / saw · didn't + verb

ex.en: I visited my aunt yesterday.
She went to Sylhet last week.
We saw a good movie.
He didn't call me.
They ate rice for lunch.

q.s: Yesterday I ___ to the market.
She ___ the letter last night.
We ___ go out because of the rain.
He ___ his keys this morning.
They ___ football two days ago.

bnsub: Simple past: অতীতে যা হয়েছিল
expbn: অতীতে শেষ হয়ে যাওয়া কাজ বলতে simple past। সাধারণ ক্রিয়ায় শেষে ed (work → worked)।
অনেক ক্রিয়ার রূপ আলাদা, এগুলো মুখস্থ করতে হয়: go → went, see → saw, eat → ate। না-বোধক করতে didn't + মূল ক্রিয়া।
rulebn: worked / went / saw · didn't + verb
sub: Finished actions in the past
exp: Use the simple past for actions that started and finished in the past. Regular verbs add -ed: work → worked.
Many common verbs are irregular and you need to learn them: go → went, see → saw, eat → ate. For negatives use didn't + the base verb: He didn't call.

rule: Do you…? · Does she…? · Did they…? + base verb

ex.en: Do you speak English?
Does he live here?
Did you eat breakfast?
Where do you work?
What did she say?

q.s: ___ your mother work?
___ you see the match last night?
Where ___ they live?
Does he ___ tea?
What time ___ the shop open?

bnsub: প্রশ্ন বানানো: do, does, did দিয়ে
expbn: সাধারণ ক্রিয়ার বাক্যকে প্রশ্ন বানাতে শুরুতে Do / Does / Did বসে, আর মূল ক্রিয়া আগের রূপে ফিরে যায় (s বা ed থাকে না)।
he / she / it হলে Does, অতীত হলে সবার জন্য Did।
rulebn: Do you…? · Does she…? · Did they…? + মূল ক্রিয়া
sub: Making questions with do, does and did
exp: To make a question with an ordinary verb, put Do, Does or Did at the start. The main verb goes back to its base form (no -s, no -ed).
Use Does with he, she or it. Use Did for the past with everyone: Did you see it?

rule: will + verb · am / is / are going to + verb

ex.en: I will call you later.
It will rain tomorrow.
We are going to buy a new car.
ex.bn: আমরা একটা নতুন গাড়ি কিনতে যাচ্ছি।

ex.en: She is going to study abroad.
I won't be late.

q.s: The phone is ringing. I ___ answer it.
We ___ visit Cox's Bazar next month. We booked the hotel.
I think it ___ be a good day.
She ___ to start a new job.
Don't worry, I ___ tell anyone.

bnsub: ভবিষ্যৎ: will আর going to
expbn: এখনই নেওয়া সিদ্ধান্ত, প্রতিশ্রুতি বা অনুমান বোঝাতে will।
আগে থেকে ঠিক করা পরিকল্পনা বোঝাতে am / is / are going to।
rulebn: will + verb · am / is / are going to + verb
sub: Talking about the future
exp: Use will for decisions you make now, promises and predictions: I will call you later.
Use am, is or are going to for plans you have already made: We are going to buy a car.

rule: can / could / should / must + base verb

ex.en: I can swim.
Could you help me?
ex.bn: আপনি কি আমাকে সাহায্য করতে পারবেন?

ex.en: You should drink more water.
You must wear a seat belt.
ex.bn: তোমাকে অবশ্যই সিট বেল্ট পরতে হবে।

ex.en: She couldn't come yesterday.

q.s: You look tired. You ___ rest.
He ___ speak three languages.
___ you open the window, please?
Students ___ cheat in the exam.
I ___ ride a bike when I was five.

bnsub: can, could, should, must: পারা, উচিত, বাধ্যতা
expbn: can = পারা (এখন), could = পারত (অতীত) বা ভদ্র অনুরোধ, should = উচিত (পরামর্শ), must = অবশ্যই করতে হবে।
এদের পরে সবসময় ক্রিয়ার মূল রূপ বসে, কোনো to বা s লাগে না।
rulebn: can / could / should / must + মূল ক্রিয়া
sub: Ability, advice and rules
exp: can = able to (now), could = was able to (past) or a polite request, should = advice, must = it is necessary or a rule.
After these words, always use the base verb, with no to and no -s: She can swim. You should rest.

rule: at 5 pm · on Friday · in July │ in the bag · on the wall · at the door

ex.en: The class starts at nine.
My birthday is on Friday.
I was born in 1998.
The keys are on the table.
I'll meet you at the station.
ex.bn: আমি স্টেশনে তোমার সাথে দেখা করব।

q.s: The meeting is ___ 3 pm.
We will travel ___ December.
The picture is ___ the wall.
I'll see you ___ Monday.
She is waiting ___ the bus stop.

bnsub: in, on, at: সময় আর জায়গা
expbn: সময়ে: at + নির্দিষ্ট সময় (at 5 o'clock), on + দিন বা তারিখ (on Monday), in + মাস, বছর, ঋতু (in May, in 2026)।
জায়গায়: in = ভিতরে (in the room), on = উপরে (on the table), at = নির্দিষ্ট জায়গায় (at the bus stop)।
rulebn: at 5 pm · on Friday · in July │ in the bag · on the wall · at the door
sub: Prepositions of time and place
exp: Time: at for exact times (at 5 o'clock), on for days and dates (on Monday), in for months, years and seasons (in May, in 2026).
Place: in = inside (in the room), on = on a surface (on the table), at = at a point or place (at the bus stop).

rule: There is + one · There are + more than one · Is there…? / Are there…?

ex.en: There is a park near my house.
ex.bn: আমার বাসার কাছে একটা পার্ক আছে।

ex.en: There are five people in my family.
Is there a bank here?
There aren't any eggs.
There was a problem yesterday.

q.s: ___ a cat under the bed.
___ many shops in this street.
___ a hospital near here?
There ___ any milk in the fridge.
There ___ two students absent today.

bnsub: There is / There are: কোথাও কিছু আছে বলতে
expbn: কোনো জায়গায় কিছু আছে বলতে there is (একটা) আর there are (অনেক)। প্রশ্নে Is there / Are there।
বাংলায় যেমন বলি “টেবিলে একটা বই আছে”, ইংরেজিতে বলি There is a book on the table।
rulebn: There is + একটা · There are + অনেক · Is there…? / Are there…?
sub: Saying that something exists
exp: Use there is for one thing and there are for more than one. In questions: Is there…? / Are there…?
Many languages start with the place (“On the table, a book is”). In English, start with there: There is a book on the table.

rule: tall → taller → the tallest · expensive → more expensive → the most expensive

ex.en: My brother is taller than me.
This phone is more expensive than that one.
Dhaka is the biggest city in Bangladesh.
She is the best student in the class.
Today is worse than yesterday.

q.s: A car is ___ than a bike.
This is the ___ day of my life.
English is ___ than math for me.
He is the ___ player in the team.
This hotel is ___ than the other one.

bnsub: তুলনা: bigger, the biggest
expbn: দুটো জিনিসের তুলনায় ছোট বিশেষণের শেষে er + than (bigger than)। লম্বা বিশেষণের আগে more (more beautiful than)।
সবার মধ্যে সেরা বোঝাতে the + est (the biggest) বা the most (the most beautiful)। ব্যতিক্রম: good → better → the best, bad → worse → the worst।
rulebn: tall → taller → the tallest · expensive → more expensive → the most expensive
sub: Comparing things
exp: To compare two things, add -er + than to short adjectives (bigger than). Put more before long adjectives (more beautiful than).
For the top one in a group, use the + -est or the most (the biggest, the most beautiful). Irregular: good → better → the best, bad → worse → the worst.

rule: many books · much water │ I have some · Do you have any? · I don't have any

ex.en: How many people came?
How much money do you need?
I bought some vegetables.
Do you have any questions?
We don't have much time.

q.s: How ___ brothers do you have?
How ___ sugar do you want?
I need ___ help, please.
Is there ___ rice left?
There aren't ___ chairs in the room.

bnsub: much, many, some, any: পরিমাণ বোঝাতে
expbn: যা গোনা যায় (books, people) তার সাথে many, যা গোনা যায় না (water, money, time) তার সাথে much।
হ্যাঁ-বোধক বাক্যে some, প্রশ্ন আর না-বোধক বাক্যে সাধারণত any।
rulebn: many books · much water │ I have some · Do you have any? · I don't have any
sub: Talking about quantity
exp: Use many with things you can count (books, people) and much with things you can't count (water, money, time).
Use some in positive sentences and any in questions and negatives: I bought some eggs. Do you have any questions?

rule: have / has + past participle (gone, seen, finished)

ex.en: I have finished my work.
She has never been to India.
Have you eaten yet?
We have lived here since 2020.
He has just left.

q.s: I ___ this movie three times.
She ___ her homework yet.
___ you ever ___ sushi?
They have worked here ___ five years.
I ___ him yesterday.

bnsub: Present perfect: অভিজ্ঞতা আর এখন পর্যন্ত
expbn: have / has + ক্রিয়ার তৃতীয় রূপ (done, seen, eaten)। অতীতে হয়েছে কিন্তু তার প্রভাব বা গুরুত্ব এখনো আছে, অথবা জীবনের অভিজ্ঞতা বোঝাতে।
নির্দিষ্ট অতীত সময় (yesterday, last year) থাকলে present perfect না, simple past বসে। already, yet, ever, never, since, for এর সাথে প্রায়ই এটা আসে।
rulebn: have / has + past participle (gone, seen, finished)
sub: Experiences and results up to now
exp: Use have or has + the past participle (done, seen, eaten) for life experiences and past actions that matter now: I have finished my work.
Don't use it with a finished time like yesterday or last year; use the simple past instead. It often goes with already, yet, ever, never, just, since and for.

rule: If + present, … will + verb

ex.en: If it rains, we will stay home.
If you study hard, you will pass.
ex.bn: কষ্ট করে পড়লে তুমি পাস করবে।

ex.en: I will call you if I need help.
ex.bn: সাহায্য লাগলে আমি তোমাকে ফোন করব।

ex.en: If she comes, I will tell her.
If we leave now, we won't be late.
ex.bn: এখন বের হলে আমাদের দেরি হবে না।

q.s: If you ___ early, you will catch the bus.
If it is sunny, we ___ to the beach.
I will be happy if you ___.
If he ___ hurry, he will miss the train.
What ___ you do if you lose your job?

bnsub: If দিয়ে শর্ত: যদি এটা হয়, তাহলে ওটা হবে
expbn: ভবিষ্যতে সম্ভব কোনো শর্ত বোঝাতে If + present, তারপর will + মূল ক্রিয়া।
If-এর অংশে will বসে না। যেমন If it rains (ঠিক), If it will rain (ভুল)।
rulebn: If + present, … will + verb
sub: If this happens, that will happen
exp: Use If + present tense, then will + verb for a possible situation in the future: If it rains, we will stay home.
Don't use will in the if part. Say If it rains, not If it will rain.

rule: is / are / was / were + past participle (made, built, written)

ex.en: This shirt is made in Bangladesh.
The bridge was built in 2022.
English is spoken in many countries.
My phone was stolen.
The results will be announced tomorrow.

q.s: Rice ___ in many parts of Asia.
The window ___ by the children yesterday.
These cars ___ in Japan.
The letter ___ last week.
The meeting ___ next Monday.

bnsub: Passive voice: কাজটা কে করেছে তার চেয়ে কাজটাই জরুরি
expbn: কাজটা কে করেছে জানা নেই বা গুরুত্বপূর্ণ না হলে passive ব্যবহার হয়: be + ক্রিয়ার তৃতীয় রূপ।
কে করেছে বলতে চাইলে শেষে by যোগ করা যায়: The book was written by Humayun Ahmed।
rulebn: is / are / was / were + past participle (made, built, written)
sub: When the action matters more than who did it
exp: Use the passive when we don't know or don't care who did the action: be + the past participle (made, built, written).
To say who did it, add by at the end: The book was written by Humayun Ahmed.

rule: If + past simple, … would + verb

ex.en: If I had a car, I would drive to work.
ex.bn: আমার গাড়ি থাকলে আমি গাড়ি চালিয়ে অফিসে যেতাম।

ex.en: If she lived near the sea, she would swim every day.
ex.bn: সে সমুদ্রের কাছে থাকলে প্রতিদিন সাঁতার কাটত।

ex.en: What would you do if you won the lottery?
If I were you, I would call him.
ex.bn: আমি তোমার জায়গায় থাকলে তাকে ফোন করতাম।

ex.en: We wouldn't go out if it rained.
ex.bn: বৃষ্টি হলে আমরা বাইরে যেতাম না।

q.s: If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.
If she had time, she ___ help us.
What would you do if you ___ your job?
If I were you, I ___ take the job.
They ___ buy a house if they had enough money.

bnsub: Second conditional: কল্পনার পরিস্থিতি
expbn: এখন বা ভবিষ্যতে যা সত্য না, বা হওয়ার সম্ভাবনা কম, এমন কাল্পনিক পরিস্থিতি বোঝাতে second conditional: If I had more time, I would learn French।
if-এর অংশে past simple, অন্য অংশে would + মূল ক্রিয়া। be হলে সাধারণত সবার সাথে were: If I were you, I would rest।
rulebn: If + past simple, … would + verb
sub: Imagining a different present or future
exp: Use the second conditional for situations that are imaginary or unlikely, now or in the future: If I had more time, I would learn French.
Use the past simple after if, and would + base verb in the other part. With be, we often use were for everyone: If I were you, I would rest.

rule: who = people · which = things · that = people or things · where = places · whose = belonging to

ex.en: The woman who called you is my aunt.
ex.bn: যে মহিলা তোমাকে ফোন করেছিলেন, তিনি আমার খালা।

ex.en: I lost the phone which I bought last week.
ex.bn: গত সপ্তাহে কেনা ফোনটা আমি হারিয়ে ফেলেছি।

ex.en: This is the town where I grew up.
ex.bn: এই সেই শহর যেখানে আমি বড় হয়েছি।

ex.en: He is the teacher that helped me most.
ex.bn: উনিই সেই শিক্ষক যিনি আমাকে সবচেয়ে বেশি সাহায্য করেছেন।

ex.en: I met a man whose son plays for Bangladesh.
ex.bn: আমার এমন একজনের সাথে দেখা হলো যার ছেলে বাংলাদেশের হয়ে খেলে।

q.s: The girl ___ won the prize is my cousin.
I like books ___ have happy endings.
This is the hospital ___ I was born.
The man ___ car was stolen called the police.
Is this the bus ___ goes to Uttara?

bnsub: who, which, that, where, whose দিয়ে বাড়তি তথ্য
expbn: নতুন বাক্য শুরু না করে কোনো ব্যক্তি বা জিনিস সম্পর্কে বাড়তি তথ্য দিতে relative clause: The man who lives next door is a doctor।
মানুষের জন্য who, জিনিসের জন্য which, মানুষ বা জিনিস দুটোর জন্যই that, জায়গার জন্য where আর কার জিনিস বোঝাতে whose।
rulebn: who = people · which = things · that = people or things · where = places · whose = belonging to
sub: Adding information with relative clauses
exp: Use a relative clause to say more about a noun without starting a new sentence: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
Use who for people, which for things, that for people or things, where for places and whose for possession: This is the café where we met. The woman whose bag was stolen called the police.

rule: If + had + past participle, … would have + past participle

ex.en: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
ex.bn: আরও মন দিয়ে পড়লে আমি পরীক্ষায় পাস করতাম।

ex.en: If we had known about the traffic, we would have left earlier.
ex.bn: জ্যামের কথা জানলে আমরা আরও আগে বের হতাম।

ex.en: She would have come if you had invited her.
If it hadn't rained, we would have played cricket.
ex.bn: বৃষ্টি না হলে আমরা ক্রিকেট খেলতাম।

ex.en: What would you have done if you had missed the flight?
ex.bn: ফ্লাইট মিস করলে তুমি কী করতে?

q.s: If I ___ the alarm, I would have woken up on time.
If they had asked me, I ___ them.
She ___ the job if she had applied.
If you ___ me, I would have come to the party.
We would have won if our best player ___ injured.

bnsub: Third conditional: অতীত অন্যরকম হলে কী হতো
expbn: অতীতে যা ঘটেনি, সেটা ঘটলে কী হতো তা বলতে third conditional, প্রায়ই আফসোস বোঝাতে: If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train।
if-এর অংশে had + ক্রিয়ার তৃতীয় রূপ, অন্য অংশে would have + ক্রিয়ার তৃতীয় রূপ। দুটো অংশই অতীতের, আর ঘটনাটা আসলে ঘটেনি।
rulebn: If + had + past participle, … would have + past participle
sub: Imagining a different past
exp: Use the third conditional to imagine a different past, often to talk about regrets: If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train.
Use if + had + past participle, and would have + past participle in the other part. Both parts are about the past, and the situation did not really happen.

rule: am / is → was · will → would · can → could · present → past · past → had + past participle

ex.en: She said she was hungry.
He told me he would be late.
ex.bn: সে আমাকে বলল তার দেরি হবে।

ex.en: They said they had finished the work.
ex.bn: তারা বলল তারা কাজ শেষ করে ফেলেছে।

ex.en: My boss said I could leave early.
ex.bn: আমার বস বললেন আমি আগে চলে যেতে পারি।

ex.en: She asked me where I lived.
ex.bn: সে আমাকে জিজ্ঞেস করল আমি কোথায় থাকি।

q.s: “I am busy,” he said. → He said he ___ busy.
“I will help you,” she said. → She said she ___ help me.
He ___ me that he was leaving.
“We have finished,” they said. → They said they ___ finished.
“Where did you go?” she asked. → She asked me where I ___.

bnsub: Reported speech: অন্যের কথা জানানো
expbn: অন্য কেউ কী বলেছে তা জানাতে reported speech। সাধারণত tense এক ধাপ পিছিয়ে যায়: “I am tired” → He said he was tired।
দরকার হলে pronoun আর সময়ের শব্দ বদলায়: tomorrow → the next day। say-এর পরে কারো নাম বা pronoun বসে না, কিন্তু tell-এর পরে বসাতেই হয়: He told me he was busy।
rulebn: am / is → was · will → would · can → could · present → past · past → had + past participle
sub: Telling someone what another person said
exp: Use reported speech to tell someone what another person said. The tense usually moves one step back: “I am tired” → He said (that) he was tired.
Change pronouns and time words when needed: “I will call you tomorrow” → She said she would call me the next day. After say, don't add a person; after tell, you must: He told me he was busy.

rule: must be = almost sure · might / may / could be = possible · can't be = almost sure it's not

ex.en: You must be hungry after that long journey.
ex.bn: এত লম্বা যাত্রার পর তোমার নিশ্চয়ই খিদে পেয়েছে।

ex.en: The door is locked. They might be out.
ex.bn: দরজা বন্ধ। তারা হয়তো বাইরে গেছে।

ex.en: That can't be Karim. He's in London.
ex.bn: ওটা করিম হতে পারে না। সে লন্ডনে।

ex.en: She must have forgotten our meeting.
ex.bn: সে নিশ্চয়ই আমাদের মিটিংয়ের কথা ভুলে গেছে।

ex.en: He might have taken the wrong bus.

q.s: He's been working for 12 hours. He ___ be tired.
I'm not sure where she is. She ___ be at the library.
That ___ be his car. His car is red, and this one is blue.
The ground is wet. It must ___ last night.
She didn't answer the phone. She ___ have been asleep.

bnsub: must, might, can't দিয়ে অনুমান
expbn: কোনো কিছু নিয়ে কতটা নিশ্চিত তা বোঝাতে: must = প্রায় নিশ্চিত হ্যাঁ, might / may / could = হতে পারে, can't = প্রায় নিশ্চিত না।
অতীতের অনুমানে have + ক্রিয়ার তৃতীয় রূপ যোগ হয়: You must have been tired। She might have missed the bus।
rulebn: must be = almost sure · might / may / could be = possible · can't be = almost sure it's not
sub: Saying how sure you are
exp: Use must, might (may, could) and can't to show how sure you are about something now: She must be at home (I'm almost sure). He might be busy (it's possible). That can't be true (I'm almost sure it isn't).
For the past, add have + past participle: You must have been tired. She might have missed the bus. He can't have seen us.

rule: had + past participle (had gone, had seen, had finished)

ex.en: When we got to the station, the train had left.
ex.bn: আমরা স্টেশনে পৌঁছানোর আগেই ট্রেন ছেড়ে দিয়েছিল।

ex.en: She had never flown before her trip to Dubai.
ex.bn: দুবাই যাওয়ার আগে সে কখনো প্লেনে চড়েনি।

ex.en: I had already eaten when he called.
ex.bn: সে যখন ফোন করল, তার আগেই আমি খেয়ে ফেলেছিলাম।

ex.en: By the time the police arrived, the thief had escaped.
ex.bn: পুলিশ আসার আগেই চোর পালিয়ে গিয়েছিল।

ex.en: He was nervous because he hadn't prepared.
ex.bn: সে প্রস্তুতি নেয়নি বলে নার্ভাস ছিল।

q.s: When I arrived, the meeting ___ already started.
She was tired because she ___ all night.
By the time we got there, everyone ___ home.
I ___ never seen snow before I went to Japan.
He couldn't pay because he ___ his wallet.

bnsub: Past perfect: অতীতের আগের অতীত
expbn: অতীতে দুটো ঘটনার মধ্যে যেটা আগে ঘটেছিল, সেটা বোঝাতে past perfect (had + ক্রিয়ার তৃতীয় রূপ): When I arrived, the film had already started।
এতে ঘটনাগুলোর ক্রম পরিষ্কার হয়। already, just, never, before, by the time-এর সাথে প্রায়ই আসে।
rulebn: had + past participle (had gone, had seen, had finished)
sub: The earlier of two past actions
exp: Use the past perfect (had + past participle) for an action that happened before another action in the past: When I arrived, the film had already started.
It makes the order of past events clear. It often goes with already, just, never, before and by the time.

en: used to / be used to / get used to
rule: used to + verb (past habit) · be used to + -ing (normal for me) · get used to + -ing (becoming normal)

ex.en: I used to play cricket every afternoon.
ex.bn: আমি আগে প্রতিদিন বিকেলে ক্রিকেট খেলতাম।

ex.en: She didn't use to like coffee.
ex.bn: আগে সে কফি পছন্দ করত না।

ex.en: I'm used to waking up early.
He is getting used to his new job.
ex.bn: সে নতুন চাকরিতে অভ্যস্ত হয়ে উঠছে।

ex.en: It took me a month to get used to the cold.
ex.bn: ঠান্ডায় অভ্যস্ত হতে আমার এক মাস লেগেছিল।

q.s: When I was a child, I ___ climb trees.
I'm used to ___ in heavy traffic.
Did you ___ live in Chittagong?
It's hard at first, but you will ___ used to it.
Working at night is normal for her. She ___ used to it.

bnsub: used to, be used to, get used to-এর পার্থক্য
expbn: used to + ক্রিয়া = অতীতে যা নিয়মিত হতো কিন্তু এখন আর হয় না: I used to live in Sylhet।
be used to + -ing = কোনো কিছুতে অভ্যস্ত: I'm used to working late। get used to = ধীরে ধীরে অভ্যস্ত হয়ে ওঠা: You will get used to the traffic।
rulebn: used to + verb (past habit) · be used to + -ing (normal for me) · get used to + -ing (becoming normal)
sub: Past habits and getting familiar
exp: used to + verb talks about past habits or situations that are not true now: I used to live in Sylhet.
be used to + noun or -ing means something is normal for you: I'm used to working late. get used to means it is becoming normal: You will get used to the traffic.

rule: enjoy / finish / avoid + -ing · want / decide / hope + to + verb · preposition + -ing

ex.en: I enjoy cooking for my family.
ex.bn: পরিবারের জন্য রান্না করতে আমার ভালো লাগে।

ex.en: We decided to leave early.
ex.bn: আমরা আগে বেরিয়ে যাওয়ার সিদ্ধান্ত নিলাম।

ex.en: He finished writing the report.
She hopes to get a scholarship.
ex.bn: সে একটা স্কলারশিপ পাওয়ার আশা করছে।

ex.en: Thank you for helping me.

q.s: I enjoy ___ to music.
They decided ___ a new car.
Please avoid ___ your phone while driving.
I'm good at ___ problems.
We need ___ more water.

bnsub: -ing নাকি to + ক্রিয়া
expbn: কিছু ক্রিয়ার পরে -ing বসে: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, keep, suggest। যেমন I enjoy reading।
কিছু ক্রিয়ার পরে to + ক্রিয়া বসে: want, decide, hope, plan, need, agree, promise। preposition-এর পরে সবসময় -ing: I'm interested in learning Spanish।
rulebn: enjoy / finish / avoid + -ing · want / decide / hope + to + verb · preposition + -ing
sub: enjoy doing or decide to do?
exp: Some verbs are followed by -ing: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, keep, suggest. I enjoy reading.
Others are followed by to + verb: want, decide, hope, plan, need, agree, promise. She decided to study abroad. After a preposition, always use -ing: I'm interested in learning Spanish.

rule: If + had + past participle, … would + verb (now) · If + past simple, … would have + past participle (then)

ex.en: If I had saved more money, I would have a house now.
ex.bn: আরও টাকা জমালে এখন আমার একটা বাড়ি থাকত।

ex.en: If she had studied medicine, she would be a doctor today.
ex.bn: সে মেডিকেলে পড়লে আজ ডাক্তার হতো।

ex.en: If he weren't so shy, he would have spoken at the meeting.
ex.bn: সে এত লাজুক না হলে মিটিংয়ে কথা বলত।

ex.en: If I spoke French, I would have understood the film.
We wouldn't be lost if we had brought a map.
ex.bn: ম্যাপ আনলে আমরা পথ হারাতাম না।

q.s: If I had slept well last night, I ___ so tired now.
If she ___ the train, she would be here now.
If he were more organised, he ___ the deadline last week.
We would be in Cox's Bazar now if we ___ the tickets.
If I ___ English as a child, I would be fluent now.

bnsub: Mixed conditional: অতীত আর বর্তমান মিলিয়ে
expbn: mixed conditional দুই সময়কে জোড়ে। অতীতের শর্ত, বর্তমানের ফল: If I had taken that job, I would be rich now।
বর্তমানের শর্ত, অতীতের ফল: If I were more careful, I wouldn't have made that mistake। প্রতিটা অংশের রূপ তার নিজের সময় দেখে বাছুন।
rulebn: If + had + past participle, … would + verb (now) · If + past simple, … would have + past participle (then)
sub: Mixing past and present in one if-sentence
exp: Mixed conditionals connect different times. A past condition with a present result: If I had taken that job, I would be rich now.
A present condition with a past result: If I were more careful, I wouldn't have made that mistake. Choose the form of each half by its own time.

rule: Never / Rarely / Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb

ex.en: Never have I eaten such delicious food.
ex.bn: এত সুস্বাদু খাবার আমি কখনো খাইনি।

ex.en: Rarely do we see snow in Dhaka.
ex.bn: ঢাকায় আমরা খুব কমই তুষার দেখি।

ex.en: Not only did he finish early, but he also helped others.
ex.bn: সে শুধু আগে শেষই করেনি, অন্যদেরও সাহায্য করেছে।

ex.en: Hardly had we arrived when it started to rain.
ex.bn: আমরা পৌঁছাতে না পৌঁছাতেই বৃষ্টি শুরু হলো।

ex.en: Under no circumstances should you share your password.
ex.bn: কোনো অবস্থাতেই পাসওয়ার্ড কাউকে দেবেন না।

q.s: Never ___ seen such a big crowd.
Rarely ___ he eat breakfast.
Not only ___ she sing, but she also plays the guitar.
Hardly had we sat down ___ the phone rang.
Under no circumstances ___ leave the door open.

bnsub: জোর দিতে উল্টো ক্রম (inversion)
expbn: ফর্মাল বা জোরালো ইংরেজিতে কিছু না-বোধক শব্দ বাক্যের শুরুতে আনা যায়, তখন সাহায্যকারী ক্রিয়া subject-এর আগে বসে: Never have I seen such a beautiful view।
এমন শব্দ: never, rarely, seldom, not only, hardly … when, no sooner … than, under no circumstances।
rulebn: Never / Rarely / Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb
sub: Never have I… / Not only… but also
exp: In formal or dramatic English, some negative or limiting words can start the sentence, and then the auxiliary comes before the subject: Never have I seen such a beautiful view.
Common starters: never, rarely, seldom, not only, hardly … when, no sooner … than, under no circumstances. Not only is she smart, but she is also kind.

rule: wish + past (now) · wish + had + past participle (regret) · wish + would (annoyance)

ex.en: I wish I lived closer to my office.
ex.bn: আহা, যদি অফিসের আরও কাছে থাকতাম।

ex.en: If only I knew the answer!
She wishes she had gone to the party.
ex.bn: সে আফসোস করছে, পার্টিতে গেলে ভালো হতো।

ex.en: I wish it would stop raining.
Do you ever wish you were taller?
ex.bn: তোমার কি কখনো মনে হয়, আরেকটু লম্বা হলে ভালো হতো?

q.s: I wish I ___ how to swim.
He wishes he ___ that car. It breaks down every week.
I wish you ___ stop interrupting me.
If only I ___ more time yesterday!
She wishes she ___ in a bigger city.

bnsub: wish আর if only দিয়ে ইচ্ছা ও আফসোস
expbn: বর্তমানের কোনো অবস্থা অন্যরকম হোক চাইলে wish বা if only + past simple: I wish I had more free time।
অতীতের আফসোসে wish + past perfect: I wish I had studied harder। কারো আচরণে বিরক্তি বোঝাতে wish + would: I wish you would stop shouting।
rulebn: wish + past (now) · wish + had + past participle (regret) · wish + would (annoyance)
sub: Wanting things to be different
exp: Use wish or if only + past simple for a present situation you want to be different: I wish I had more free time. (I don't have enough.)
Use wish + past perfect for past regrets: I wish I had studied harder. Use wish + would to complain about someone's behaviour: I wish you would stop shouting.

rule: What I need is … · It was … who / that …

ex.en: What I love about Dhaka is the food.
ex.bn: ঢাকার যে জিনিসটা আমার সবচেয়ে ভালো লাগে, তা হলো খাবার।

ex.en: It was my sister who taught me to cook.
What we need is more time.
ex.bn: আমাদের যা দরকার তা হলো আরও সময়।

ex.en: It was in 2020 that we moved here.
What surprised me was how friendly everyone was.
ex.bn: আমাকে যা অবাক করেছে তা হলো সবাই কত বন্ধুসুলভ।

q.s: ___ I want is a quiet weekend.
It was my father ___ gave me this watch.
It was in Sylhet ___ we first met.
What she needs ___ a good rest.
___ was the price that surprised me.

bnsub: Cleft sentence: গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অংশে জোর দেওয়া
expbn: একটা বাক্যকে দুই ভাগ করে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অংশে জোর দিতে cleft sentence: What I need is a holiday। It was Karim who found the mistake।
জিনিস বা কাজে জোর দিতে What … is / was, আর মানুষ, সময় বা জায়গায় জোর দিতে It is / was … that / who।
rulebn: What I need is … · It was … who / that …
sub: What I need is… / It was… who
exp: Cleft sentences split one idea into two parts to put the focus on the important information: What I need is a holiday. It was Karim who found the mistake.
Use What + clause + is / was … to highlight a thing or an action. Use It is / was … that / who … to highlight a person, a time or a place.
